title: Protocol for using negative pressure isolator systems to study BSL-2 organisms in gnotobiotic murine models
protocol: Prepare Trans-Tainer transfer containers in a sterilizing cylinder in the home isolator.
Set up prepared cages in the experimental negative-pressure BSL-2 isolator before transferring mice.
Transfer three germ-free mice from their home isolator to the experimental isolator.
Allow transferred mice to acclimate for one week.
Monitor the sterility of the isolator and supplies using germ-free mice.
Confirm the sterility of the isolator and supplies before proceeding with further transfers.
Turn off negative pressure when transferring animals to avoid exerting too much pressure on the inner port cover.
Prepare Trans-Tainer tubes by placing one filter cap on.
Add a small amount of bedding and pellets of diet to each tube.
Use forceps to hold mice at the base of the tail.
Gently lift and place mice in the Trans-Tainer tube(s), ensuring not to mix litters.
Securely fasten the end cap to the open end of the tube.
Set a timer for 20 minutes to minimize time spent in the tube.
Remove the band and inner port cover from the isolator port.
Place the Trans-Tainer tube(s) in the port quickly.
Replace the inner port cover and band immediately after placing the tubes.
Remove the outer port cover and take out the Trans-Tainer tube(s).
Prepare the experimental negative-pressure BSL-2 isolator to receive mice.
Turn off negative-pressure airflow by closing the valve.
Remove the outer port cover.
Place the Trans-Tainer tube(s) in the port.
Thoroughly spray all surfaces of the tube(s) and the port with Clidox®-S.
Spray the outer port cover, replace, and fog the port with Clidox®-S.
Set a timer for 15 minutes to allow Clidox®-S to sterilize the port and tubes.
Monitor the mice for signs of distress.
Remove the Trans-Tainer tube(s) from the port if mice display signs of distress.
Break one tab on the filter cap to remove it.
Turn negative pressure airflow back on after 15 minutes.
Pull the mice in through the inner port cover.
Open a prepared cage and one end of the Trans-Tainer tube by breaking a tab.
Move the tube to cover the cage, angling the open side down so that mice move into the cage.
Close the cage and observe the mice for 1 or 2 min to ensure normal behavior.
Distribute mice to other cages as needed by picking them up by the base of the tail using forceps.
Use long forceps to gently lift one mouse from the cage by the base of the tail and place into a tri-corner beaker.
Wait approximately 5 minutes for the mouse to produce two fecal pellets.
Label one microcentrifuge tube with the appropriate isolator number/letter and date.
Gently remove the fecal pellets from the beaker using forceps and place them into a snap-cap tube.
Place the sample tube containing fecal pellets into the transfer port of the isolator, then close the inner port cover securely.
Remove the sample tube from the outer port cover once the inner port cap is fastened securely.
Sterilize and close the port following step 15 f in “before you begin” procedure.
Homogenize the collected fecal pellet sample in 900 μL of pre-reduced 1× PBS with 0.05% cysteine.
Pipette 100 μL of the homogenized sample onto a blood agar plate and streak evenly across the surface.
Pipette another 100 μL of the homogenized sample onto a Brucella agar plate and streak evenly.
Incubate both blood agar plates aerobically at 37°C for 24 hours.
Incubate the Brucella plates anaerobically in an anaerobic chamber at 37°C for 48 hours.
Vortex fecal homogenate briefly to resuspend.
Pipette 10 μL of the homogenate onto a glass slide and allow it to dry.
Heat-fix the sample by quickly passing the slide over a flame several times.
Flood the slide with Gram Crystal Violet and let sit for 1 min.
Rinse the slide gently with water, avoiding direct stream contact with the sample.
Flood the slide with Gram Iodine and let sit for 1 min.
Thoroughly rinse the slide with decolorizing solution consisting of 30% acetone and 70% ethanol until it runs clear.
Rinse the slide thoroughly with water.
Flood the slide with Gram Safranin and let sit for 30 seconds.
Thoroughly rinse the slide with water and allow it to dry.
Observe the slide at 400–1000× magnification with a light microscope.
Confirm the absence of bacterial or fungal cells from germ-free samples and that mono-associated mice are free from contamination by other bacteria or fungi.
Wear cotton gloves over the isolator gloves when handling animals in the isolator to provide better grip.
Spray the commensal inoculum Hungate tube and 1 mL syringe with safety needle with freshly prepared Clidox®-S.
Allow 30 min of exposure to Clidox®-S before pulling the items into the isolator.
Open the 1 mL syringe and carefully pierce the septum of the Hungate tube to draw up the inoculum.
Seal needle in the safety cap.
Remove the capped needle and replace it with the gavage tube.
Pick up a mouse by the base of the tail using forceps and place on the cage lid.
Restrain the mouse by holding by the skin at the nape of the neck, hold upright, and place the tail between the 4th and 5th fingers to hold firmly.
Carefully introduce the gavage tube into the mouth and then into esophagus.
Once the tube is placed, carefully inject 200 μL of inoculum.
Carefully remove the tube and return the mouse to its cage.
Observe mouse for up to 5 min for normal behavior.
Collect fecal pellets from mice after 48 h.
Administer 200 μl of C. difficile spores at a dose of 1 × 10^3 CFU via gavage.
Measure body weight using a tri-corner beaker on the scale weighing tray.
Pick up mouse with forceps and place in the beaker for weighing.
Record the stable weight once the mouse is settled.
Return the mouse to its cage after weighing.
Observe mice for C. difficile infection symptoms and general signs of pain and distress.
Evaluate prior recorded weights when assigning a body condition score.
Euthanize mice if they attain a score of 2- due to significant weight loss or severe distress.
Ensure all required equipment for BSL-2 waste management is available before starting.
Contain all materials and instruments in the isolator in double autoclavable biohazard bags.
Spray autoclavable biohazard bags and steam integrator strips with freshly prepared Clidox®-S through the isolator port.
Replace outer port cover as described in the section “before you begin” step 15f.
Allow 15 min of contact time before pulling items into the isolator.
Collect cages, cups, feeding needles, and other instruments in a double biohazard bag with a chemical integrator strip.
Tie off each bagged item securely.
Collect all bedding, diet, and other disposable material in a separate double biohazard bag.
Collect scale in a separate double biohazard bag.
Remove the inner port cover from the isolator.
Remove a rubber stopper from the outer port cover.
Fog the chamber and materials with Clidox®-S sterilant using an atomizer through the opening.
Allow 5 hours for contact sterilization to occur.
Pull bagged waste and materials out of the isolator.
Dispose of waste in the appropriate biohazard waste containers.
Sterilize the bagged scale by ethylene oxide sterilization.
Ensure the dosimeter indicates the cycle has completed before removing the scale from the bag.
Break down isolator components and contain them appropriately.
Turn off positive pressure air pumps by unplugging power supply.
Disconnect filters by loosening hose clamps and screws, then detach from the isolator.
Remove vinyl tape and plastic covers.
Spray all surfaces of plastic covers with Clidox®-S sterilant.
Allow 30 minutes for contact time before wiping.
Place filter frames in a double autoclavable biohazard bag.
Double knot to close the bag containing filter frames.
Decontaminate bagged cages, instruments, and filter frames by autoclaving at 129°C and 30 PSI for at least 20 minutes.
Ensure that steam integrator strips indicate the cycle has passed.
If not, re-autoclave until properly sterilized.
